title: Throughput notes & weekly priorities — personal ledger
content:
Purpose:
This is my working ledger for weekly priorities, lightweight OKR tracking and quick retros. Primary goal: keep my execution aligned to team throughput goals (tickets closed, rollout velocity, and reduction in per-token cost for canary routes) while protecting focus time for deep work on kernel selection experiments.

Weekly snapshot (week of 2025-03-03 -> 2025-03-09):
- PRs opened: 4 (two were small bugfixes, one instrumentation add, one kernel-selection prototype)
- PRs merged: 3 (missing one review from SRE blocking merge)
- Incidents triggered: 0 (good)
- Time spent on meetings: ~7.5 hours (too high; target <= 6h)
- Deep work blocks hit: 5 blocks of 90-120m each (target 6)
- Personal throughput metric (deliverable-complete count): 3/5 planned deliverables this sprint.
- Mini-KPI: Reduced average 95p latency of model-x canary by ~8% during A/B run (preliminary).

Quick notes on metrics:
- 95p latency reduction seems correlated with KV cache pruning and smaller batch size for short prompt paths. Need to run controlled A/B purely toggling cache pruning to isolate.
- Cost metric: per-token cost moved down ~2% — likely noise. Do not call victory yet.

Wins this week:
- Got instrumentation merged that shows queueing time per worker; immediately exposed a mis-sized prefetch buffer on one pool. Action item already in the PR thread.
- Mentor session with Katelin was useful; refined my approach to choosing default batching heuristics.
- Kept incident free on the night shift rotation. Felt less reactive.

Blockers / unresolved:
- SRE review lagging on runtime PR #1124 (linked above). Needs sign-off before I can roll canary to dedicated. Pinged Ravi but it's still open.
- Elastic autoscaler test failing intermittently in CI. Failing step: integration test of graceful draining. Ticket: ENG-4823.
- Need clarity from product on acceptable latency SLO for the new small-model tier (email to product sent 2025-03-06; no reply).

Action items (this sprint / next week):
- A1: Isolate KV cache pruning experiment (controlled A/B) — create small dataset, run 2 full-day experiments, collect 95p and cost deltas. (owner: me)
- A2: Follow up with SRE on PR sign-off. If no response by 2025-03-12, escalate to on-call lead and add small clarifying test to unblock. (owner: me)
- A3: Draft short one-pager for product with proposed small-model latency SLO options and tradeoffs. (owner: me, review: Katelin). Target: 2025-03-14.
- A4: Reduce meeting time by 1.5 hours/week: propose biweekly sync cadence change with infra team; share agenda + pre-reads. (owner: me)

Personal OKR checkpoint (quarter goal alignment):
- Objective: Improve core-serving reliability & cost efficiency for medium-latency tiers.
  - KR1: Reduce median end-to-end latency for 'model-x-medium' by 15% by end of Q2. Current: baseline -> median 210ms, after recent changes -> 195ms. Progress: ~12% relative improvement toward KR.
  - KR2: Deliver 3 experiments that save >=10% per-token CPU cost for at least one production workload. Current experiments: KV pruning (prelim +8%), lightweight quantization path (benchmarks pending), batch-size tuning (mixed results).
  - KR3: Ship automated rollout with rollback on metric regression for one critical route. Status: canary infra in place; missing SRE sign-off.

Hypotheses / experiment ideas (brainstorm):
- H1: If we enable prefix-specific caching (per top-10 prompt templates) then we will reduce token compute by ~6–10% for common query shapes; risk: cache invalidation complexity.
- H2: Dynamic batch shaping: use a short-window model to predict token-length distribution and adapt batch-size at 10s intervals — could reduce tail latency for short prompts. Complexity: adds another tuning knob.
- H3: Aggressive KV eviction policy for cold sessions reduces memory pressure and yields fewer OOMs during burst traffic; cost: slight performance hit for long context sessions.

Retro: what to do differently next week:
- Block proactively: add a small "blocking checklist" to PR templates to speed SRE review.
- Timebox meetings: pre-reads must be shared 24h before; decline if no agenda.
- Prioritize one deep experiment per week; small follow-ups can be done in short slots.

Notes to self / friction points:
- I notice I default to adding too many metrics into a single graph. Break out signal into separate dashboards for latency, queue, and CPU to avoid correlation confusion.
- Mental model: treat canary rollouts like fragile experiments — have clear rollback criteria and an owner for the first 48 hours.

Quick calendar + reminders:
- 2025-03-11 10:00am: 1:1 w/ Katelin (prep: share one-pager draft)
- 2025-03-12 EOD: follow-up on SRE sign-off (if not signed)
- 2025-03-14: finish product SLO one-pager
- 2025-03-18: start day-1 KV pruning controlled run

Loose thread ideas (capture for later):
- Could write a short devblog about the kernel selection heuristics tradeoffs; useful for internal onboarding and recruiting.
- Small checklist for canary owners to include in console (steps, metrics to watch, rollback anchor).

End note: keep this doc messy and writable. Weekly on Fridays I will add a 5-minute summary and move obvious done items to a private board (not yet set up).

---
Version history (quick):
- 2025-02-11: initial notes + draft OKRs
- 2025-02-25: added experiment ideas after reading kernel perf notes
- 2025-03-03: weekly snapshot added
- 2025-03-10: updated with A/B results and action items
